title: Steelers NFL Draft: Denzel Boston Pick Analysis & Latest News
text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are entering the 2026 NFL Draft with a clear need at wide receiver, and Denzel Boston of Southern Cal is quickly emerging as a potential early target. Boston’s combination of size, reliable hands, and ability to win contested catches makes him an intriguing prospect for a team looking to add a physical presence to their passing game.
At 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds, Boston possesses the frame to thrive in a physical NFL receiving corps. Scouts consistently praise his ability to box out defenders and come down with the ball in traffic. This skill set is particularly valuable in the red zone and on crucial third-down conversions, areas where the Steelers have sought improvement. He consistently demonstrates the ability to craft difficult catches, often securing the ball even with tight coverage, a trait that has drawn comparisons to established NFL receivers known for their physicality.
A Deep Dive into Boston’s Skillset
Beyond his size, Boston’s route running has developed significantly throughout his collegiate career. While not known for elite speed, he utilizes his body effectively to create separation and consistently finds soft spots in zone coverage. His ability to adjust to poorly thrown balls is also a notable strength, making him a dependable target for quarterbacks. He finished his final season at USC with 68 receptions for 987 yards and 11 touchdowns, showcasing his ability to be a primary receiving threat.
What sets Boston apart is his willingness to engage in physical battles for the ball. He doesn’t shy away from contact and consistently fights for position, making him a nightmare for defensive backs. This competitive edge is something Steelers coaches reportedly value highly, particularly in a division known for its physical play. His contested catch rate during his time at USC was consistently above 60%, a testament to his strength and determination.
How Boston Fits with the Steelers’ Offensive Needs
The Steelers’ current receiving group features Diontae Johnson, but the team is looking for a receiver who can consistently win one-on-one matchups and provide a reliable target in the red zone. Boston’s skillset aligns well with this need. He could complement Johnson’s route-running ability with his size and physicality, creating a more versatile and dynamic passing attack.
Analysts suggest that Boston could be available when the Steelers select at pick number 20 in the draft, though his stock has been steadily rising in recent weeks. Several mock drafts now project him as a first-round pick, potentially requiring the Steelers to trade up to secure his services. The team has reportedly been conducting extensive interviews with Boston, signaling a strong level of interest.
Potential Concerns and Draft Outlook
While Boston possesses many desirable traits, some scouts have raised concerns about his top-end speed and ability to consistently create separation against elite cornerbacks. However, his strengths – size, hands, and physicality – are considered more valuable in the modern NFL, where contested catches and red-zone production are highly prized.
The Steelers have a history of drafting receivers who excel in these areas, and Boston appears to fit that mold. If available at pick 20, he would likely be a strong contender for the Steelers’ first-round selection. The team’s evaluation process will continue in the coming weeks, but as of now, Denzel Boston represents a compelling option to bolster their receiving corps.
The NFL Draft is scheduled for April 23-25 in Detroit. Fans can identify more information about the Steelers’ draft strategy and potential targets on the team’s official website.
